edits.value_json: 上 means “above” or “up”; its early graph is interpreted as a positional mark above a reference line. The early line is described as curved in some accounts and horizontal in others.

上 is an indicative graph, not a compound of semantic or phonetic components. Its early construction is interpreted as a short mark above a reference line to indicate the upper position; sources differ on whether some early lines were curved or horizontal. This historical analysis describes the earlier construction, not a decomposition of the present strokes. The received Shuowen text also classifies 上 as indicative, a Han-era analysis rather than independent confirmation of the earlier history.

Reported Shang-period examples include 上帝, 上甲, and contrasts with 下; Zhou bronze examples include spatial “above.” These support early spatial uses as well as the current sense, but do not establish priority among every lexical use.
Current dictionary definitions include rank-related “superior”; its historical sequence relative to spatial “above” is not established.
